questions.question: Explain why the VOC and colonists used slave labour at the Cape.
questions.expected_answer: Labour was scarce; bringing European workers was expensive (they expected wages); the VOC forbade enslaving the Khoikhoi, on whom it depended for trade, and the Khoikhoi were unwilling to work permanently for the Dutch; free burgher farmers from 1657 needed workers; slavery was already normal in VOC Asian territories; growing wine and wheat farming increased demand.

questions.question: Where did enslaved people at the Cape come from?
questions.expected_answer: Africa (West Africa and Angola in 1658, later Mozambique and the East African coast); Madagascar (a major source); India (Coromandel, Bengal, Malabar) and Sri Lanka (Ceylon); Indonesia/South-East Asia (Java, Bali, Sulawesi, Timor) - often called 'Malays'. Roughly a quarter from each region; later many were Cape-born (creole).

questions.question: Describe how enslaved people were brought to and treated on arrival at the Cape.
questions.expected_answer: Captured in wars, raids and kidnappings, enslaved for crimes or debts, or sold in famine; bought by VOC slaving voyages (Madagascar, Mozambique) for guns, gunpowder, cloth, beads, copper and alcohol; brought on returning VOC ships from Asia or sold by foreign ships; crowded, chained, deadly voyages; sold at auction or privately, examined like livestock and given new names (e.g. September, Van Bengalen); VOC slaves housed in the Slave Lodge.
